questions.prompt: Which evaluation best tests the robustness of a domain-randomized controller?
options: Parameters at the extremes outside the training box, with worst-case and failure counts
Fresh samples from the same training box, reporting only the mean cost
The nominal plant only, reporting its cost to many decimals
The training cost at the last iteration, averaged over the box
questions.explanation: Fresh samples from the same box measure interpolation. Robustness to the unmodelled needs points outside the box and worst-case reporting.

questions.prompt: A payload is 3.0 kg with 20% tolerance. What is the lower end of the sampling range? (one decimal)
Three parameters, each randomized with 2 bins per axis. How many cells are there in the coverage grid?
Probability that 20 independent uniform samples all miss a region with 10% of the volume? (three decimals)
Compared with controller gains tuned on the nominal plant only, gains tuned over a randomized box typically
options: only matter for sensor noise, not for plant parameter changes
are better at every parameter value, including the nominal plant
cost a little at the nominal plant and cut the worst-case cost
are worse at every parameter value, including the extremes
questions.explanation: They are a compromise: slightly worse where the nominal controller was optimal, much better where it was fragile.

questions.prompt: Explain why ranges that are too wide can be as harmful as ranges that are too narrow.
rubric: Too narrow: the real robot lies outside the box, no robustness
Too wide: conservative policy, lower performance, harder training
Ranges should come from measurement tolerance and physical reasoning, tested by held-out extremes
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Describe how you would decide the ranges for mass, friction and latency of a mobile robot and what you would hold out for testing.
rubric: Uses measurements, datasheet tolerances or system identification to set each range
Treats multiplicative parameters (friction) on a log or relative scale
Holds out extreme combinations outside the box and reports worst case
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
